title: Kelly Gulch cabin, Topanga (Pumpkinhead 1988)
description: The cabin where the teenagers hide out after the accident that kills Billy Harley was shot at Kelly Gulch, a frequently filmed property at 1801 North Topanga Canyon Boulevard. The same cabin played the Jarvis house in Friday the 13th: The Final Chapter. It is a private residence, look from the sidewalk only, and there is no public access to the grounds.

title: Vermont Canyon Tennis Courts, Griffith Park, Los Angeles (The Howling 1981)
description: Karen and Donna play tennis here, and Sheriff Sam Newfield reassures them about the creature they heard in the woods. The scene is set at the Colony but was shot on a court at 2715 North Vermont Canyon Road, in the south of Griffith Park. The courts are a public city tennis facility, so visitors can go.

title: Site of Eddie Quist's house, Garland Avenue, Los Angeles (The Howling 1981)
description: Chris and Terry search Eddie Quist's room, its walls covered in drawings, in an old Queen Anne house that stood on this block of Garland Avenue between 7th and 8th Streets, behind 1200 West 7th Street. The house was demolished right after filming in 1980 and nothing of it remains. The pin marks the block, not an exact lot; it is a public city street.

title: Delta Street, Ladner Village, Delta (Trick 'r Treat 2007)
description: Delta Street in historic Ladner Village stood in for the downtown streets of Warren Valley, Ohio. Today it is a working village main street of shops and restaurants. It is a public street and visitors can walk it freely.

title: West 36th Avenue at Carnarvon Street, Vancouver (Trick 'r Treat 2007)
description: The location site Horror Explorer matches this residential corner to the film's school bus and Wrong Way sign shots. It sits several blocks east of the houses used on West 36th Avenue. It is a public street corner in a quiet neighborhood; the surrounding homes are private residences, look from the sidewalk only.

title: North Shore Studios (formerly Lions Gate Studios), North Vancouver (Trick 'r Treat 2007)
description: Several sets were built on stage at the Lionsgate lot, now North Shore Studios, at 555 Brooksbank Avenue. A set visit report describes a full mine shaft for the quarry story and a re-creation of the back of Mr. Kreeg's house and his neighbor Steven's yard. It is a working studio lot and is not open to visitors.

title: The stranger's house, Yeoun Village, Seokgok-myeon, Gokseong (The Wailing 2016)
description: The Japanese stranger's hideout, the house Jong-goo smashes up while shouting at him to leave, is the last house at the far end of this tiny mountain village. The production restored an abandoned house for the shoot and it still stands empty. The national tourism listing says the site is open at all times, but the neighboring homes are private residences, so park at the village hall, walk in quietly and go in daylight.

title: Guseongjae Pass, Ogok-myeon, Gokseong (The Wailing 2016)
description: The scene where the truck carrying Jong-goo and his friends hits the stranger's body was filmed on this winding mountain pass road. Today it is a popular driving and cycling route with an octagonal pavilion and viewpoint at the top. It is a public road, open year round.

title: Eupnae Police Substation, Gokseong-eup (The Wailing 2016)
description: This small police substation on Jungang-ro in central Gokseong served as the station where officer Jong-goo works. It is still a working police post. Visitors can see the exterior from the street but should not go inside to sightsee.

title: Gokseong Catholic Church, Gokseong-eup (The Wailing 2016)
description: The church where Jong-goo meets the priest while trying to uncover the stranger's secret is Gokseong Catholic Church. It is an active parish church in the town center. Visitors can see the grounds respectfully outside of services.

title: Dongsan riverside fishing spot, Dongsan-ri, Gokseong-eup (The Wailing 2016)
description: The film's opening scene, with the stranger fishing at the water's edge, was shot at the Dongsan fishing spot on the Seomjin River. Navigation apps list it as Dongsan Yuwonji, a quiet riverside recreation area. It is a public riverbank and visitors can go.

title: Gokseong Metasequoia Road, Gokseong-eup (The Wailing 2016)
description: Jong-goo and his daughter Hyo-jin ride his motorbike down this avenue of tall metasequoia trees. The tree-lined stretch lies on the road into Gokseong-eup from the Namwon side and is a well known scenic drive. It is a public road, so take care with traffic when stopping for photos.

title: Docheon Village, Byeonggok-myeon, Hamyang (The Wailing 2016)
description: The house where the shaman Il-gwang stages his ritual, Jong-goo's family home in the film, is not in Gokseong but in this farming village in Hamyang County, where the crew filmed the day and night ritual scenes over several days. The pin marks the village hall, not the house. The house is a private residence, look from the sidewalk only; the village lanes are public and pleasant to walk.

title: Maewoldae Falls, Geunnam-myeon, Cheorwon (The Wailing 2016)
description: The stranger's ritual bathing under a waterfall was filmed here in mid September, after the producers could not find a deep enough waterfall in the south of the country. The falls sit on the slopes of Bokgyesan and are one of Cheorwon's listed scenic sights. It is a public hiking destination, open at all times, reached by a rough mountain trail.

title: Moraejae Pass road, Jinan (The Wailing 2016)
description: The drone shot of a winding mountain road when the shaman Il-gwang first appears was filmed on the national road over Moraejae Pass. The producer says the team wanted a road that winds like a snake, ringed by layers of mountains. It is a public road and visitors can drive it.

title: Masonic Home of Washington (Landmark on the Sound), Des Moines, Washington (The Ward 2010)
description: Exterior shots of the North Bend Psychiatric Hospital were filmed at this 1920s Masonic retirement home at 23660 Marine View Drive South, while the hospital interiors were shot in eastern Washington. The building has been vacant for years and the owner's demolition permit was upheld in 2026, so it may be fenced off or already coming down. It is private property and not open to visitors, view it from the public road only.

title: Boardwalk at 14th Street, Ocean City, New Jersey (Servant 2019)
description: Apple TV crews filmed beach and boardwalk scenes for a season 3 episode near 14th Street in March 2021, according to the city's spokesman. About 65 cast and crew were based at the nearby Flanders Hotel for the shoot, though the filming itself was on the sand and the boards. The boardwalk is a public place and free to walk.

title: Fort Langley Community Hall, Fort Langley, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: The production dressed this hall as the White Pine Bay Woodchuck Festival for an overnight shoot in October 2012, used in season 1 for Norma's date with Deputy Shelby. It is a working community hall at 9167 Glover Road that is rented for events. The exterior can be seen from the street at any time.

title: Horseshoe Bay Park, West Vancouver, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: The waterfront park was dressed as White Pine Bay for crowd scenes in season 2 episode 4, and Dylan's talk with his uncle Caleb was filmed the same day on a dock at the marina beside it. Horseshoe Bay doubled for the town from the first season on. It is a public park next to the ferry terminal and free to visit.

title: Bay Market, Horseshoe Bay, West Vancouver, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: For season 1 episode 7 the crew turned this corner grocery into Bay Market and Hardware, where Norman and Dylan buy supplies at a fall hardware sale and run into Bradley outside. The shop sits at 6414 Bruce Street on the corner with Royal Avenue. It is a business on a public street, so the storefront is easy to see from the sidewalk.

title: Horseshoe Bay Motel, West Vancouver, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: This motel played The King's Motel in season 2 episode 4, where Norma sits in her Mercedes staring up at her brother Caleb's room and Norman later goes in to confront him. It is a real motel at 6588 Royal Avenue. A condo redevelopment has been proposed for the site, so check that it is still standing, and view it from the street unless you are a guest.

title: Troll's Restaurant, Horseshoe Bay, West Vancouver, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: Romero and Dylan's meeting about how dangerous Norman has become, in the season 4 episode Forever, was shot here in long takes in March 2016. Troll's is a restaurant at 6408 Bay Street and open to the public. A hotel redevelopment of this corner has been approved, so check that it is still trading before you go.

title: Steveston Fisherman's Wharf, Richmond, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: In November 2012 the show filmed on the Steveston docks and a fishing boat for season 1 episode 4, where Sheriff Romero and Deputy Shelby are called out after a fisherman finds a hand in his net. White Pine Bay County Sheriff cars were parked on the docks for the shoot. The wharf is a public working dock that visitors can walk for free.

title: Britannia Shipyards National Historic Site, Steveston, Richmond, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: A regular location for the series. In season 2 episode 9 Norma runs down the walkway to a locked door and screams to see Dylan, a scene Vera Farmiga repeated at least a dozen times here in November 2013. It is a national historic site and public waterfront park at 5180 Westwater Drive, open to visitors.

title: Dave's Fish and Chips, Moncton Street, Steveston, Richmond, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: In November 2014 a block of Moncton Street was turned into White Pine Bay for season 3, with Norma parking her green Mercedes outside Dave's Fish and Chips while Caleb unloads his jeep a little to the east. The restaurant at 3460 Moncton Street is a business open to the public. The same block is better known as Storybrooke in Once Upon a Time.

title: Seycove Secondary School, North Vancouver, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: Seycove Secondary played Norman's high school in the series. It is a working public school at 1204 Caledonia Avenue in the Deep Cove area. It is not open to visitors, so view the exterior from the street and stay off the grounds during school hours.

title: Vancouver Art Gallery, Vancouver, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: Norman's murder trial in the final season, in the episode that aired April 17, 2017, was filmed in the old law courtroom inside this former courthouse. The building is now the Vancouver Art Gallery at 750 Hornby Street. The exterior is free to see at any time, and gallery admission applies inside.

title: 2400 Motel, Kingsway, Vancouver, British Columbia (Bates Motel 2013)
description: The 2400 Motel appears in season 1 episode 8, according to a location blogger who matched it against screenshots from the episode. It is a working motor court at 2400 Kingsway that has been used by many other productions. The city plans to redevelop the site, so check that it is still standing, and view it from the street unless you are a guest.

title: 128 Park Road, Toronto, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: This house is the exterior of the Thompson home in Let's Get Invisible (1996), the only exterior location in that episode, and it returns as Aunt Dahlia's house in An Old Story (1997). The attic with the mirror is believed to have been a studio set. It is a private residence, look from the sidewalk only.

title: Silver Springs Farmhouse, 7960 Reesor Road, Markham, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: This brick farmhouse from the 1870s played the O'Dell house in Night of the Living Dummy III, and was also a location for the 1980 horror film Funeral Home. It was bought by a numbered company in 2022 and designated a heritage property in 2024. It is a private residence, look from the sidewalk only, which here means the public roadside, and do not enter the grounds.

title: Lawrence Park Collegiate Institute, Toronto, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: This is the school in Phantom of the Auditorium, and it appears again, flipped horizontally, as the school in It Came From Beneath the Sink. It is a working public high school at 125 Chatsworth Drive. It is not open to visitors, so view the exterior from the street.

title: Serena Gundy Park, East York, Toronto, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: The park stood in for the HorrorLand grounds in One Day at HorrorLand, and its bridge appears in Werewolf Skin. It is a public city park reached from Rykert Crescent. It is free to visit.

title: Sunnybrook Park, North York, Toronto, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: A repeat location for the series: Muddy Creek in You Can't Scare Me, the curvy road in Welcome to Dead House, the stables in Werewolf Skin, and scenes in The Barking Ghost and Perfect School were all shot in this park. It is a large public park at 1132 Leslie Street. It is free to visit.

title: Cawthra Estate, Mississauga, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: The mansion played Hill House, the haunted tour house in The Headless Ghost. The Cawthra Estate at 1507 Cawthra Road is owned by the City of Mississauga and used as an event venue. Visitors can see the exterior from outside, and the interior is open only for booked events.

title: York Mills Collegiate Institute, North York, Toronto, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: This building was used as the school in three episodes: Go Eat Worms, My Best Friend Is Invisible and Say Cheese and Die Again. It is a working public high school at 490 York Mills Road. It is not open to visitors, so view the exterior from the street.

title: Factory Theatre, Toronto, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: This is the theatre in Bride of the Living Dummy. It is the home of Factory Theatre, a working playhouse at 125 Bathurst Street. The exterior can be seen from the street at any time, and you can go inside by buying a ticket to a show.

title: Bluffer's Park Beach, Scarborough, Toronto, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: The beach in the episode Ghost Beach was filmed here, at the foot of the Scarborough Bluffs. It is a public beach inside Bluffer's Park. It is free to visit.

title: Milne Dam Conservation Park, Markham, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: The park scenes in Go Eat Worms were filmed here. It is a public conservation park at 8251 McCowan Road. It is open to visitors during park hours.

title: Cedar Grove Mennonite Cemetery, Reesor Road, Markham, Ontario (Goosebumps 1995)
description: This is the graveyard seen in The Haunted Mask, named Eda Grove Cemetery in the location guide. It is the Cedar Grove Mennonite Cemetery at 7452 Reesor Road, a real burial ground. Visit quietly in daylight and treat it with respect.

title: West High School, Salt Lake City (Hereditary 2018)
description: The school interiors, including Peter's classroom scenes, and the scene of Charlie with the dead bird were filmed at West High School. It is a working public high school at 241 North 300 West. It is not open to visitors, so view it from the public sidewalk only.

title: Grand Building, Utah State Fairpark, Salt Lake City (Hereditary 2018)
description: The exterior of the high school, in the scene where Joan shouts at Peter from across the street, was filmed beside the Grand Building at the Utah State Fairpark. The Fairpark at 155 North 1000 West is a public event venue. The source found the grounds open on its visit, though access can change with events.

title: Pioneer Building, Utah State Fairpark, Salt Lake City (Hereditary 2018)
description: This building played the exterior of the grief support group where Annie first meets Joan. It stands on the Utah State Fairpark grounds at 155 North 1000 West, a public event venue. The source found the grounds open on its visit, though access can change with events.

title: Utah Film Studios, Park City (Hereditary 2018)
description: The interiors of the Graham house were built as sets on the soundstages here, which gave the film its dollhouse look. The exterior of the art supply store, where Annie runs into Joan in the parking lot, was also shot on the studio grounds. Utah Film Studios at 4001 Kearns Boulevard is a working, gated facility and is not open to visitors.

title: Kearns Boulevard at Comstock Drive, Park City (Hereditary 2018)
description: The moment where Steve nearly runs a light and brakes hard was filmed at this intersection. It is an ordinary public road junction in Park City that anyone can drive or walk past.

title: Perfection town set site, off Cactus Flats Road, Olancha (Tremors 1990)
description: The town of Perfection, with Walter Chang's Market, the street and the houses, was built as a set in the open desert off Cactus Flats Road outside Olancha and torn down after the 1989 shoot. Nothing stands today: only faint dirt tracks of the old layout show in aerial imagery. It is remote, unpaved desert with no services, and the land ownership is not confirmed, so stay on the public road.

title: Santa Monica Pier entrance, Colorado Avenue at Ocean Avenue, Santa Monica (The Entity 1982)
description: The scene where the entity takes control of Carla's car and sends it out of control was filmed at the entrance gate to Santa Monica Pier, where Colorado Avenue meets Ocean Avenue. The arched pier sign and the ramp down to the pier are still there. It is a public landmark that anyone can visit.

title: Bord Gáis Energy Theatre, Grand Canal Square, Dublin (Abigail 2024)
description: Abigail's opening ballet performance, danced alone on the stage, was filmed in this theatre. It is a working venue in the Dublin Docklands. The square outside is public, and the auditorium is open to ticket holders on show nights.

title: Sir John Rogerson's Quay, Dublin (Abigail 2024)
description: The Dublin Docklands doubled for the film's American city, and the night driving scenes of the kidnap crew's getaway were filmed along this quay on the south bank of the Liffey. It is a public street and riverside walk, open to everyone.
